note: Original factual annotations. Event URLs cite dates and claims; coordinates locate the named place approximately, not battlefield boundaries. BC dates use astronomical years (1 BC = 0).

items.title: Rome sacked
items.text: Alaric’s forces sacked Rome in AD 410.

items.title: Western deposition
items.text: Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in AD 476. Ravenna locates the western court; this conventional endpoint did not end all Roman institutions.
items.source: Met, The Roman Empire; UNESCO Ravenna

items.title: Eastern survival
items.text: Constantinople remained the seat of Roman imperial government. Justinian’s sixth-century rule belongs to this continuing eastern history.

items.title: Crusader conquest
items.text: The Fourth Crusade captured Constantinople in 1204 and established a Latin empire.

items.title: Imperial restoration
items.text: Constantinople returned to Byzantine imperial rule in 1261.

items.title: Ottoman conquest
items.text: The Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453 ended its Byzantine imperial government.
